767955.trap: Agitation and hyperthermia suggest amphetamine intoxication, but nystagmus is the hallmark physical sign of PCP.

nodes.text: Acute psychotic agitation, violent combativeness, and paranoia: check vital signs and pupil/eye findings
Identify PCP hallmarks: multidirectional or horizontal nystagmus, myoclonus, analgesia, and autonomic arousal
Place patient in a calm, low-stimulation environment to minimize sensory triggers
Administer IV or IM benzodiazepines (lorazepam, diazepam) as first-line for agitation and seizures
**Severe agitation refractory to benzodiazepines:** add low-dose haloperidol cautiously
Monitor for life-threatening complications: rhabdomyolysis, hyperthermia, seizures, and trauma
**CK markedly elevated or dark urine:** aggressive IV crystalloid hydration to protect kidneys
Serial observation until toxicity resolves
